text:
David Perron is 38, has had 11 NHL stints with eight teams (St. Louis three times, Detroit twice), and now has a goal for Dallas. It came in the 8-3 loss to Winnipeg on Nov. 12, the first in six games as a Star, on a night he took six shots in 14 and a half minutes.

He's in a small role, 11 minutes a night, and the sample is too small to judge. What we can say is that he's still getting to good ice: 1.17 individual expected goals per 60 so far, well above last season's 0.63. The Stars have been worse at five on five with him on, but six games of shot share tells you almost nothing.

The value Evolving-Hockey saw in him last season was defensive: 1.5 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength defense, with opponents getting fewer chances when he was out there (94th percentile). He was never fast and isn't now (bottom 1% for top speed), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 24% of his entries. He wins with hands and positioning. He has 812 career points and a 2019 Stanley Cup.
